The internal screen shows screen_candidate_k=1 for all four candidate sets, with large leading eigengaps (0.73–0.96) and small secondary gaps, so the dominant spectral resolution is the single-cluster resolution and no dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal is present. This is a screening result only: partition-level screening does not provide actual feasible k>=2 solutions or their measurements, and absence of subdivision is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates. Within-set affinities are positive and exceed all between-set affinities, and the nearest-pair affinities identify K5_C0002–K5_C0003 as the closest boundary (0.151), followed by K5_C0001_M_K5_C0005–K5_C0002 (0.138). These are candidate-generation consensus geometry quantities, not external validation or stability scores, and the nearest-pair entries are a review entry point rather than a merge conclusion. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, with no dominant internal subdivision signal and uniformly lower between-set than within-set affinity.
